MapLibre, Mapbox, security and privacy

Source: vignettes/articles/security.Rmd
security.Rmd

MapLibre and Mapbox

All the examples use maplibre() with free basemaps, so they run without an account or token. Everything also works with mapboxgl(): create the map with your own Mapbox token as usual in mapgl. maplore never reads or stores tokens.

If you use Mapbox, your token is exposed

Any map made with mapboxgl() includes your Mapbox token in the HTML, with or without maplore: the browser needs it to load the map, so anyone who opens the page can find it. Mapbox designs public tokens for this, but someone could use yours and spend your quota. To publish Mapbox maps:

  • use a public token (pk.…), never a secret one (sk.…);
  • create a separate token for published maps, because the default public token cannot be restricted, and restrict it to your site’s URLs in your Mapbox account;
  • keep tokens in .Renviron, out of version control.

To avoid tokens altogether, use maplibre() with a free basemap. See Mapbox’s guide on using Mapbox securely.

Your data travels inside the HTML

mapgl embeds the whole sf object in the page, with every column, even the ones the map does not show. Anyone with the file can read them. With sensitive data, keep only the columns you need before mapping, for example with dplyr::select(name, value).

What maplore itself does

  • It inserts every text (names, labels) as plain text, never as HTML, so data cannot inject code into the page.
  • It makes no network requests and stores nothing in the browser.
  • It has no JavaScript dependencies of its own.
